item.title: Mendrisio-Melano, MeMe project to reduce highway noise
item.description: The Federal Office of Roads (USTRA) has published the design for the MeMe project, a comprehensive rehabilitation plan for the stretch of the A2 motorway between Mendrisio and Melano.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - MeMe Project for acoustic rehabilitation of A2 between Mendrisio and Melano - Design publication until 13 October in the municipalities of Val Mara and Mendrisio - Interventions on asphalt, noise barriers and treatment of stormwater - Work start expected as soon as possible from 2031
## Key facts Project: MeMe Section: A2 between Mendrisio and Melano Publication deadline: 13 October Promoting authority: Federal Roads Office (USTRA) Work start: from 2031 (optimistic scenario) Mentioned cost: 100 million francs
The Federal Roads Office (USTRA) has made official the publication of the design for the MeMe project, a comprehensive rehabilitation plan that concerns the section of the A2 motorway located between Mendrisio and Melano. The document can be consulted in the municipalities of Val Mara and Mendrisio until 13 October. The primary objective of the intervention is the acoustic rehabilitation of a section where the noise limit values are currently exceeded, particularly between the Lenaccio area and the Orto il gelso area.
### Technical details of the interventions
The plan foresees the use of sound-absorbing pavement and the adjustment of the existing noise barriers. To reduce acoustic impact, the existing protections will be raised by about 2 meters through the installation of glass walls. In addition to acoustic aspects, the MeMe project includes the construction of three new facilities for stormwater treatment, located respectively at the height of Sovaglia, next to the Lenaccio viaducts and in the Campaccio area.
The project does not only address noise and environment, but also intervenes on safety infrastructure. The adaptation of the emergency lane on the Lenaccio viaducts and the rehabilitation of the access ramps to the rest areas of Segoma are planned. These measures are described by USTRA as necessary to adapt the motorway section to the required standards, while ensuring a more efficient management of water and road safety in the affected section. ## Implications for cross-border commuting The stretch of A2 between Mendrisio and Melano represents a key axis for thousands of workers who cross the border each day to reach their workplaces in the Canton of Ticino. Any structural intervention on this segment directly affects the quality of life and traffic flow for those holding a G permit and traveling these roads. Although the goal is noise reduction, carrying out work of such magnitude inevitably involves a transition phase that cross-border workers will have to manage.
### Timing analysis and alternatives A critical fact emerges from the timelines communicated by USTRA: the works, in the best case, may begin from 2031. This means that for the coming years the current situation will remain unchanged. Moreover, the MeMe project is defined as a temporary measure. USTRA has in fact specified that the possibility of tunnelling the entire motorway segment in the future is not excluded, although such an operation would not occur before 2055.
For the cross‑border worker planning their movements, this means that the current sound‑recovery solution is the only concrete short‑ and medium‑term answer to prevent the population and those passing through from being exposed to noise levels above those specified by the OIF. The temporary nature of the project suggests that the infrastructure will continue to evolve, but the timeframe for more radical changes (such as the tunnel) is extremely far away.
### Criticisms and doubts about the project The project has already raised political questions. Councillor Andrea Rigamonti highlighted some criticisms through an inquiry, questioning the investment's effectiveness. In particular, it was asked what the State Council's position is regarding a plan that, despite an estimated cost of 100 million francs, would not guarantee compliance with noise limits at more than 40% of control points. This fact raises doubts about the real ability of the project to permanently solve the noise problem for those living and working along this road axis.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). Transit management and operational steps
For cross‑border workers who commute daily between Mendrisio and Melano, it is essential to monitor the evolution of the MeMe project, especially ahead of the future construction phase. Although work is not expected to start before 2031, planning traffic flows during the adaptation of emergency lanes and the laying of sound‑absorbing asphalt will be crucial to avoid delays at the border crossings and along the A2.
What to do and how to monitor
Those interested in technical details or wishing to provide feedback on the project design can visit the municipalities of Val Mara and Mendrisio by the deadline of 13 October. This is the official public consultation window. After this phase, the project will move into subsequent technical planning and final approval stages before actual execution.
For cross‑border workers, attention will shift to mobility management. Ahead of future road works, it is advisable to assess the impact such interventions could have on travel times. item.description: In 2024 the average annual salary in Lombardy rises to 30,384.07 euros, but almost half of the workers do not exceed 25,000 euros.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - In 2024 the employee base rises to 3,776,242 units with a 1.55% growth - The average annual salary is 30,384.07 euros with a 3.65% increase - Almost half of workers do not exceed the threshold of 25,000 euros per year
Employment growth: plus 1.55% compared to 2023 Average annual salary: 30,384.07 euros Nominal salary increase: plus 3.65% Workers under 20,000 euros: 1,380,567 units, equal to 36.56% of the total Workers under 25,000 euros: 49.66% of the overall base
The new report drawn up by UIL Lombardia, entitled Lombardy and Provinces - The value of work. Salaries, continuity and quality of work in 2024 and based on INPS Observatory data, highlights that despite a nominal growth in wages and employment, the Lombardy labor market continues to conceal deep inequalities and situations of marked precariousness. During 2024, the overall base of dependent workers belonging to the non-agricultural private sector rises to 3,776,242 units, recording an increase of 1.55% compared to the previous year. At the same time, the average annual salary reaches 30,384.07 euros, marking a 3.65% increase in nominal terms. However, this average figure tends to mask a much more complex and uneven internal reality for workers in general. Within the regional framework, in fact, as many as 1,380,567 workers, corresponding to 36.56% of the total base, fail to exceed the threshold of 20,000 gross euros per year. The situation appears even more critical if we consider that almost one worker in two, equal to 49.66% of the total, earns a total of less than 25,000 gross euros per year. As underlined by Antonio Albrizio, General Secretary of UIL Lombardia, the report confirms that the recorded economic growth must necessarily translate into a higher quality of work and a much more balanced distribution of the wealth produced. For the trade union organization, stable wages and good employment must remain at the center of regional policies to prevent economic expansion from leaving behind large segments of the working population. On the general economic front, the data highlight how the numerical progression of the employed does not automatically correspond to an improvement in real living conditions for all active employees in the Lombardy area, requiring a careful analysis of the contractual and salary dynamics that characterize the various provinces and various local economic sectors, with particular reference to the categories most exposed to economic vulnerability and contractual discontinuity during the twelve months of the reference year. ### Difficulties for young people and gender differences
The structural criticalities of the Lombard labour market particularly affect the most vulnerable groups, starting with the new generations and the female component. According to the report prepared on the basis of the findings of the INPS Observatory, over 1.38 million workers remain confined below the threshold of 20 thousand euros per year, and among young people up to 34 years of age this proportion widely exceeds 50%, specifically reaching 50.31% of employees under 35. Salvatore Monteduro, UIL Lombardy Confederal Secretary, highlights that the main problem is not only how many workers appear in official statistics, but how much income, continuity and autonomy can really produce the work offered by the regional economic system. Analyzing in detail the condition of young employees, who represent 33.22% of the total regional audience with about 1.25 million individuals, a picture of strong precariousness emerges: 50.31% do not exceed 20,000 euros per year and 65.18% remain permanently below 25,000 euros per year. In a region characterized by a particularly high cost of living, this persistent economic gap drastically limits the concrete possibility for young people to achieve effective housing and family autonomy, delaying emancipation and personal stability.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Sectoral analysis and necessary interventions
The strong economic polarization of the Lombardy labor market is confirmed by the wage gap between the various productive sectors, a disparity exceeding 54,000 euros per year among the economic activities considered. It ranges from an average of 67,750.86 euros recorded in the Finance and Insurance sector to a mere 13,215.45 euros found in the Accommodation and Food Service sector. In this very tourism and catering sector, economic precariousness assumes particularly significant dimensions, given that 76.20% of employees fail to reach the minimum threshold of 20,000 gross euros per year. Dario Esposito, Coordinator of UIL Lario, highlights how these regional data find particularly concerning confirmation in the Como area as well, where wages, which are on average lower than the Lombardy average, constantly contend with a steadily rising cost of living. In the Como area, work is not lacking, but too often it fails to guarantee sufficient income, contractual stability, and concrete opportunities to plan one's future, feeding a dangerous spiral of precariousness that specifically penalizes young people, women, and workers employed in the most fragile economic sectors. To reverse this negative trend, trade unions reiterate the need to intervene decisively on employment quality, strengthening national collective bargaining agreements, taking targeted action against involuntary part-time work, and promoting active policies to increase wages and job stability at the territorial level. To delve deeper into one's wage situation and accurately analyze the data relating to one's professional and social security classification, it is possible to check simulations and economic parameters using the online [calculator](nav:calculator).

## In brief - New Cross-Border Worker Agreement in effect from January 1, 2024. - Tax exemption increased to CHF 10,000 for new cross-border workers. - Withholding tax is deducted in Switzerland, with tax credit in Italy.
## Key facts New Cross-Border Worker Agreement: January 1, 2024 Ratification Italy: Law 83 of 13/6/2023 Double Taxation Convention: December 9, 1976 Old Cross-Border Worker Exemption: CHF 7,500 (until 2033) New Cross-Border Worker Exemption: CHF 10,000 Swiss Withholding Tax: Deducted in Switzerland Italian Tax Credit: Section CE of the 730 form
Transferring residency to an Italian border municipality like Brenta, with the aim of working in Ticino, requires careful consideration of several factors, chief among them the impact of the new Cross-Border Worker Agreement, which came into effect on January 1, 2024. This agreement, signed on December 23, 2020, and ratified by Italy with Law 83 of June 13, 2023, introduces significant changes compared to the previous regulations. The Double Taxation Convention between Italy and Switzerland, dated December 9, 1976, continues to represent the reference regulatory framework, but the new agreement modifies some practical aspects for cross-border workers. One of the most relevant changes concerns the tax exemption: for the so-called «new» cross-border workers, meaning those who were not already active in Ticino before July 17, 2023, the threshold for exemption from Ticino cantonal tax has been raised to CHF 10,000. For «old» cross-border workers, who retain the right to the CHF 7,500 exemption, a transitional regime is foreseen which will extend until 2033. It is fundamental to understand that the withholding tax on employment income is deducted exclusively in Switzerland. Italy, to avoid double taxation, grants a tax credit, which cross-border workers can claim by completing section CE of the 730 form. This mechanism ensures that income earned in Switzerland is not taxed twice. The choice to reside in Brenta, as in other neighboring municipalities, is often dictated by the search for a potentially lower cost of living compared to Ticino, while maintaining geographical proximity that allows for manageable commute times. However, it is essential to analyze in detail transport costs, infrastructure, and tax specifics to make an informed decision. The goal is to balance the economic benefits derived from working in a high-income market like Ticino with daily needs and tax obligations in the country of residence. ### Implicazioni Fiscali e Previdenziali: Dettagli per il Frontaliere La gestione fiscale per chi vive a Brenta e lavora in Ticino è un aspetto cruciale, influenzato dal nuovo Accordo sui frontalieri. L'imposta alla fonte, prelevata direttamente dalla busta paga svizzera, si basa su aliquote che variano in funzione del reddito e dello stato civile. Per i contribuenti con un reddito annuo lordo fino a CHF 148'200, è applicata un'aliquota che tiene conto anche della deduzione per la franchigia (CHF 10'000 per i nuovi frontalieri, CHF 7'500 per i vecchi). Oltre a queste imposte dirette, i lavoratori dipendenti devono considerare i contributi sociali svizzeri. L'AVS/AI/IPG ammonta al 5.3% del salario lordo, a cui si aggiunge l'1.1% per AD/AC (fino al cap di CHF 148'200). La LAINF (assicurazione contro gli infortuni non professionali) varia tra lo 0.7% e l'1.5%, mentre la LPP (Cassa Pensione) ha aliquote progressive, a partire dal 7% per la fascia d'età 25-34 anni, fino a superare il 18% per le fasce più anziane, applicata sulla parte di salario eccedente il minimo LPP. Sul versante italiano, l'IRPEF prevede un'aliquota del 23% per scaglioni di reddito fino a €28'000, che sale al 35% per redditi tra €28'001 e €50'000, e al 43% per quelli superiori a €50'000. La convenzione contro le doppie imposizioni, tramite il credito d'imposta, evita che il reddito venga tassato due volte, ma è essenziale una corretta dichiarazione dei redditi in entrambi i paesi per ottimizzare il carico fiscale complessivo. Per quanto riguarda l'assicurazione malattia (LAMal), i frontalieri con permesso G hanno diritto di optare per l'assicurazione svizzera o quella italiana. Se si sceglie la LAMal, è possibile beneficiare di franchigie adulte che vanno da CHF 300 a CHF 2'500, con un impatto diretto sul premio mensile. La scelta tra le due opzioni assicurative dipenderà dalle esigenze personali, dalla composizione familiare e dai costi associati.

## In brief - Bally crisis: boutique closures and bankruptcies - Total shutdown of activities in Caslano - Another 25 laid off in administration - Red balances with millions in losses
Buyer fund: Regent LP Production site: Caslano Procedure company: Transliq AG Dismissals: 25 workers Current employees: 54 staff members 2024 Loss: 60.5 million 2025 Loss: 27.7 million
The trajectory of the historic luxury brand Bally has marked a new and dramatic chapter, marked by bankruptcy procedures, boutique closures, and failed attempts to sell the brand over the past two years. Ever since US investment fund Regent LP took over the company in August 2024, the situation has taken a complex turn culminating in the total shutdown of production activities at the Ticino site in Caslano. Concern among workers and former employees has reached extremely high levels following the latest official announcements.
### The new collective dismissal procedure
According to the latest reports from the newspaper laRegione, the company Transliq AG — tasked with managing the delicate phase of the composition moratorium — has announced a new collective dismissal procedure. This measure risks directly hitting another 25 administrative workers, in what many fear may not be the last round of cuts. The downsizing of the company's footprint in the region appears merciless in its numbers when looking at the recent evolution of the brand's workforce in Canton Ticino.
### The reduction of the workforce in Caslano
Originally, Bally employed 169 people across Switzerland, with as many as 122 employed right at the Caslano plant. Out of about 100 employees still present in June, the situation has further plummeted, dropping to just 54 staff members. Added to this figure is a dozen collaborators still active in the Swiss retail network. A drastically compromised employment picture that puts at risk historic professional skills tied to the Ticino region and local manufacturing tradition. The workforce downsizing and the production halt in Caslano represent a heavy blow to the local economic fabric and to the workers revolving around Canton Ticino. The evolution of the corporate crisis shows how fragile employment stability in the manufacturing and luxury sectors can be in the face of changes in ownership and complex financial management like that of the US fund Regent LP. For those who work or have worked at the plant, the debt-restructuring moratorium managed by Transliq AG opens a phase of extreme uncertainty, in which every single administrative and production job is called into question. ### Financial data and the collapse of the accounts To confirm the severity of the picture are the company's accounts recorded over the last three years. After a positive EBITDA of 43.5 million francs in 2023, 2024 marked a vertical collapse ending with a red of 60.5 million. In 2025 the loss partially reduced to 27.7 million, but the operating cash flow remained widely negative by 16.45 million francs. These numbers explain the speed with which the situation moved from relaunch attempts to the closure of production activities and personnel cuts. ### The sales plan and the future of the plant To attempt to save operations, a sales process for the production facility was launched within the framework of the moratorium. The operation aims at the transfer of the Caslano site, including plants, lease agreements, and employment contracts, with the primary objective of resuming production and protecting local jobs. Excluded from the negotiation, however, is the brand, which is fresh from two previous acquisition attempts that ended in nothing. This separation between the brand and the production infrastructures represents the last card left to preserve the Swiss structure and give a future to the remaining employees, pending the outcome of ongoing negotiations.

Moving to Veniano for those who choose to work in Canton Ticino represents a strategic logistical solution for many commuting professionals. The geographical position in the Como area allows for a careful evaluation of road and highway connections to border crossings, facilitating daily travel to major Ticino economic centers such as Mendrisio, Lugano, and Chiasso. Analyzing travel times and road conditions is essential before planning a change of residence, taking into account the transient traffic that characterizes peak hours along the highway routes.

Frontier workers must carefully consider how their net income is affected by tax and social security deductions applied across the border, comparing them with the purchasing power guaranteed in the Italian territory of residence. The regulatory and fiscal framework governing the status of frontier workers between Italy and Switzerland is governed by the New Agreement on Frontier Workers, which entered into force on 1 January 2024 after its signature on 23 December 2020 and Italian ratification with Law 83 of 13 June 2023. With regard to the taxation of income from employment, the tax at source is withheld directly in Switzerland, while Italy eliminates double taxation through the tax credit mechanism declared in the EC framework of model 730. This method guarantees a clear distribution of the tax levy between the two Contracting States, surpassing the old regimes and offering greater legal certainty to taxpayers.

## In breve - Imposta alla fonte trattenuta solo in Svizzera - Nuovo Accordo Frontalieri in vigore dal 1° gennaio 2024 - Franchigia di 10.000 euro per i nuovi frontalieri - Esenzione di 7.500 euro per i vecchi frontalieri
## Fatti chiave Accordo Frontalieri: firmato 23/12/2020, in vigore 01/01/2024 Ratifica Italia: Legge 83 del 13/06/2023 Convenzione doppie imposizioni: 09/12/1976 Franchigia nuovi frontalieri: 10.000 euro Esenzione vecchi frontalieri: 7.500 euro
Il trasferimento a Veleso per chi lavora nel Canton Ticino richiede l'analisi di precise norme fiscali e amministrative. Il quadro normativo attuale è definito dal Nuovo Accordo Frontalieri, firmato il 23 dicembre 2020 ed entrato in vigore il 1° gennaio 2024, dopo la ratifica italiana avvenuta con la Legge 83 del 13 giugno 2023. Questo accordo ridefinisce i parametri di tassazione per chi risiede in Italia e lavora in Svizzera.
### La struttura fiscale per il residente a Veleso Per un lavoratore che risiede a Veleso, l'imposta alla fonte sul reddito da lavoro viene trattenuta esclusivamente in Svizzera. L'Italia evita la doppia imposizione attraverso l'applicazione di un credito d'imposta, che viene gestito nel quadro CE della dichiarazione dei redditi 730. Questo meccanismo è coerente con la Convenzione per l'eliminazione delle doppie imposizioni firmata tra Italia e Svizzera il 9 dicembre 1976.
L'amministrazione di tali imposte è affidata all'Amministrazione Federale delle Contribuzioni (AFC/ESTV) a livello federale e alle rispettive amministrazioni cantonali. È importante sottolineare che enti come l'Ufficio Federale di Statistica (BFS) o l'Ufficio Federale delle Assicurazioni Sociali (UFAS) non hanno competenza nella fissazione delle aliquote fiscali, ma si occupano rispettivamente di rilevazioni statistiche e previdenza sociale. Il frontaliere che sceglie Veleso come dimora deve quindi coordinare i propri obblighi tra l'AFC svizzera e l'Agenzia delle Entrate italiana per l'ottimizzazione del credito d'imposta. ## Analisi pratica e scenari
La scelta di vivere a Veleso comporta l'applicazione di regimi fiscali differenti a seconda della data di inizio dell'attività di frontaliere. I cosiddetti 'vecchi frontalieri', ovvero coloro che possedevano già tale status prima del 17 luglio 2023, beneficiano di un regime transitorio che copre il periodo 2024–2033, con un'esenzione di 7.500 euro. Al contrario, i 'nuovi frontalieri' possono usufruire di una franchigia di 10.000 euro.
### Impatto sulle trattenute e previdenza Il salario percepito in Ticino è soggetto a diverse trattenute previdenziali obbligatorie. I contributi AVS/AI/IPG ammontano al 5.3% a carico del dipendente, mentre l'assicurazione disoccupazione (AD/AC) incide per l'1.1%, con un tetto massimo di 148.200 CHF. La previdenza professionale (LPP) varia tra il 7% e il 18% a seconda della fascia d'età, partendo dai 25 anni, mentre la LAINF oscilla tra lo 0.7% e l'1.5%.
Per quanto riguarda la salute, i frontalieri con permesso G hanno diritto d'opzione per l'assicurazione malattia LAMal. Le franchigie per gli adulti variano da 300 a 2.500 CHF. Questo sistema permette di gestire la copertura sanitaria in modo flessibile, a seconda delle necessità individuali e della preferenza tra il sistema svizzero o quello italiano.
### Confronto con la fiscalità italiana Il reddito prodotto in Svizzera, una volta detratte le imposte alla fonte, deve essere confrontato con le aliquote IRPEF italiane per l'eventuale integrazione o per il calcolo del credito d'imposta. Le aliquote attuali prevedono il 23% fino a 28.000 euro, il 35% tra 28.001 e 50.000 euro, e il 43% per le quote eccedenti i 50.000 euro. Un frontaliere che risiede a Veleso deve quindi monitorare costantemente il proprio reddito complessivo per evitare sorprese in fase di dichiarazione dei redditi, utilizzando strumenti di [calcolo fiscale](nav:calculator) per simulare il netto reale.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ## Guida all'azione per il trasferimento
Chi decide di trasferirsi a Veleso per lavorare in Ticino deve seguire una procedura precisa per regolarizzare la propria posizione amministrativa e fiscale. Il primo passo è l'ottenimento del permesso G, che attesta lo status di frontaliere e permette l'accesso ai diritti d'opzione per la LAMal e l'applicazione del regime fiscale di frontiera.
### Step operativi per il frontaliere 1. Richiesta del Permesso G: l'istanza va presentata alle autorità competenti del Canton Ticino per formalizzare il rapporto di lavoro transfrontaliero. 2. Scelta dell'assicurazione sanitaria: decidere se aderire alla LAMal svizzera (scegliendo la franchigia tra 300 e 2.500 CHF) o mantenere la copertura italiana. Per approfondire i costi, è possibile consultare la guida su [LAMal e CMI](nav:health). 3. Configurazione previdenziale: verificare che i contributi AVS e LPP siano correttamente versati in busta paga secondo le fasce d'età previste. 4. Gestione fiscale: in occasione della dichiarazione dei redditi in Italia, inserire i dati del reddito svizzero nel quadro CE del modello 730 per richiedere il credito d'imposta e neutralizzare la doppia imposizione.
### Considerazioni logistiche e costi Il pendolarismo da Veleso verso i centri produttivi ticinesi richiede una pianificazione dei tempi di percorrenza e dei costi di trasporto. È consigliabile valutare l'impatto delle spese di viaggio sul salario netto, considerando l'uso dell'auto e l'eventuale acquisto della vignetta autostradale. item.description: Asst Seven Lakes denies the blockade of the third lot of the Del Ponte Hospital of Varese. Loans of 13.6 million already in cash and work started.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Asst Sette Laghi replies to the open letter from the Municipality - The blocking of the third lot is categorically denied - Financing of 13.6 million euros already in the cash register - Development of the maternal and child hub regularly underway
## Key facts - **What**: Institutional reply on the future of the Del Ponte Hospital - When: September 2026 - Where: Varese, Filippo Del Ponte Hospital - Who: Asst Sette Laghi and Palazzo Estense - Amount: 13.6 million euros
The Varese healthcare company Asst Sette Laghi has issued an official note to directly respond to the open letter delivered to the regional Welfare department by the mayor of Varese and the executive board of Palazzo Estense. At the center of the debate is the future of the Filippo Del Ponte Hospital and, in particular, the construction and completion of the third lot of the Varese healthcare facility. The healthcare company's reply was clear and left no room for interpretation regarding the rumors circulating in recent days.
In the official note released by the Varese health management, it is defined as completely false that a decision has been made not to complete the third lot of the Del Ponte Hospital. On the contrary, the company strongly reiterates that the development path of the maternal-child hub continues without interruption and that a significant part of the intervention already enjoys secure financial coverage. Specifically, the resources amount to 13.6 million euros, are already present in the cash register, and have partly already been used for the first interventions launched in the field.
### Details of financing and available resources
The economic resources amounting to 13.6 million euros will continue to be used over the next two and a half years according to a defined schedule. Thanks to these funds, it was possible to create the new medically assisted procreation facility, known as PMA, as well as the new gynecological outpatient clinics. The thus renovated structure will be fully operational by the end of 2026, offering new service standards to users who turn to the healthcare hub for women's and children's health. Also in the autumn of the current year, the installation of the new Magnetic Resonance Imaging system within the Varese hospital facility is scheduled.
Within the same financial resource package, a specific budget excerpt entirely dedicated to the renovation of the facade of the Michelangelo pavilion has also been obtained. According to what was communicated by Asst Sette Laghi, the construction sites for this specific intervention will officially start by 2026, while the completion of the works is scheduled for the end of 2027. This construction site is considered fundamental not only to improve the overall functionality of the building, but also to restore a decorous image to the structure that is fully adequate to the value of the clinical and healthcare services provided daily by the medical and healthcare staff. ### Analysis of structural and logistical interventions
The management of the remaining portion of the multi-million funding is enabling the healthcare company to plan and launch the preparatory works essential for the construction of a new building within the hospital complex. In operational detail, the plan involves the creation of a new facility dedicated to staff locker rooms and the company canteen. These are infrastructural works of absolute technical necessity, as they are preparatory to the subsequent phases that will involve the demolition of the Octagon Pavilion and the start of construction of the new building foreseen by the original master plan.
The Regional Welfare Department and Asst Sette Laghi itself unanimously share the extreme strategic importance held by the Del Ponte Hospital in the Lombardy and interregional healthcare panorama. The structure is not simply considered as a local pediatric hub, but as a true highly specialized regional reference center for the protection of women's and children's health. The clinical skills and professionalism present within the hospital represent an absolute excellence, a source of pride for the healthcare company which publicly acknowledges the historical role played over the years by civil society, voluntary associations, and all the subjects who have concretely supported the growth and enhancement of the healthcare offer.
### Three-year planning and continuity of public funds
Precisely by virtue of the centrality and strategic value of Del Ponte, the company management emphasizes that its development must be pursued maintaining a vision characterized by farsightedness, administrative responsibility, and rigorous managerial common sense. The company categorically denies the existence of alleged waivers of the additional funding necessary for the overall completion of the third lot. On the contrary, the remaining share of economic resources to finalize the intervention is stably included within the official three-year programming of the Lombardy Region.
The management of Asst Sette Laghi firmly reiterates that there is no block of public funds destined for the work, nor any intention to back down from the approved projects for the third lot. The primary objective shared with the regional institutions is to avoid any form of dispersion of the public resources already committed, planning with the utmost attention and technical caution the future steps necessary to complete the entire construction site without unjustified delays.

The structural modernization program of the Del Ponte Hospital is already fully underway and operational on multiple fronts. The new medically assisted reproduction (PMA) facility has been completed, the opening of the new gynecological outpatient clinics is confirmed by the end of 2026, the start of preparatory construction sites for the new building is imminent, and the redevelopment work on the facade of the Michelangelo pavilion will begin within the current year with completion scheduled for the end of 2027. Asst Sette Laghi, benefiting from the constant support of the Lombardy Region, intends to continue building the future of local healthcare step by step, based on the firm conviction that every investment aimed at the health of women, newborns, children, and adolescents represents a fundamental investment for the well-being and development of the entire local community and its catchment areas.
The administrative and managerial action of the healthcare company will therefore continue under the banner of transparency and institutional collaboration with local and regional authorities, maintaining a strong focus on compliance with the announced timelines for each active construction site within the Varese hospital facility. item.title: New €10,000 deductible for border workers from Casalzuigno
item.description: The New Frontier Agreement in force since 2024 introduces a deductible of €10,000 for new residents in Italy working in Ticino.
item.content:encoded:
## In breve - Nuovo Accordo Frontalieri in vigore dal 1° gennaio 2024 - Franchigia esenzione nuovi frontalieri: 10.000 euro - Convenzione doppie imposizioni firmata il 9 dicembre 1976 - La Svizzera non è membro dell'UE o dello SEE
## Fatti chiave - **Cosa**: Entrata in vigore del Nuovo Accordo Frontalieri - Quando: 1° gennaio 2024 - Dove: Confine Ticino-Italia (Casalzuigno/Mendrisio) - Chi: Governi italiano e svizzero - Importo: Franchigia 10.000 euro per nuovi frontalieri
Il 23 dicembre 2020 è stata la data in cui i governi italiano e svizzero hanno firmato il nuovo Accordo Frontalieri, un testo normativo che ha ridefinito le regole fiscali per chi vive in Italia e lavora in Ticino. Questo accordo, che ha richiesto anni di negoziati, è ufficialmente in vigore dal 1° gennaio 2024, segnando una svolta per i residenti di comuni come Casalzuigno. La ratifica italiana è avvenuta con la Legge 83 del 13 giugno 2023, mentre la base giuridica risale alla Convenzione sulle doppie imposizioni firmata il 9 dicembre 1976. È fondamentale chiarire che la Svizzera non fa parte dell'Unione Europea né dello Spazio Economico Europeo, un dettaglio che incide sulle procedure burocratiche e sui diritti di residenza per chi cerca di stabilirsi nel cantone senza lavorare.
### La separazione fiscale tra i due Paesi Il meccanismo fiscale per i frontalieri si basa su una netta distinzione tra la trattenuta alla fonte e le imposte dirette. La trattenuta alla fonte sul reddito da lavoro è operata esclusivamente in Svizzera: il datore di lavoro svizzero detrae l'imposta direttamente dalla busta paga. L'Italia, dal canto suo, evita la doppia imposizione attraverso il credito d'imposta, che viene inserito nel quadro CE della dichiarazione dei redditi, il famoso 730. Questo significa che l'imposta versata in Svizzera viene rivalutata in Italia, evitando che lo stesso reddito venga tassato due volte in piena misura.
Per chi vive a Casalzuigno, vicino al confine con Mendrisio, le implicazioni sono dirette. La geografia del confine ticinese, con valichi come Brogeda, facilita il pendolarismo quotidiano. Tuttavia, le regole fiscali non conoscono la distanza chilometrica: contano la residenza e il luogo di lavoro. I vecchi frontalieri, ovvero coloro che già operavano in questo regime prima del 17 luglio 2023, godono di un regime transitorio che si estende fino al 2033, mantenendo un'esenzione di 7.500 euro. I nuovi frontalieri, invece, rientrano nella disciplina del nuovo accordo con una franchigia di 10.000 euro. Questa distinzione temporale crea due classi di contribuenti con obblighi e vantaggi diversi, un aspetto che chi si trasferisce oggi da Casalzuigno deve considerare con attenzione prima di firmare un contratto di lavoro in Ticino. ### The practical impact of the tax exemption The difference between the 7,500 euro exemption for old cross-border commuters and the 10,000 euro exemption for new ones is not just a number on a form. Represents the minimum tax base that is not taxed. For a Casalzuigno resident starting a business in Ticino from 2024, the higher deductible means that a larger part of the net income will be exempt from Italian tax. This mechanism, defined by the New Frontier Agreement, aims to make the Ticino labour market more competitive for those residing in Italy. The Convention of 9 December 1976 remains the legal basis, but the 2020 agreement updates its operational clauses.
Tax management requires precise knowledge of the entities involved. The federal and cantonal rates, as well as the tax at source, are established by specific laws and administered by the AFC/ESTV at the federal level and by the cantonal tax administrations. It is not the task of the UFAS, which deals with social security like the AVS and AI, nor of the BFS, which deals with statistics, to set these rates. Many border workers make the mistake of confusing the roles of these entities, going to ask the wrong entity for tax information. For those who live in Casalzuigno, the proximity to the border makes commuting sustainable, but the tax complexity requires relying on official channels to avoid compilation errors.
###
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Operational procedure for the transfer For those who decide to move to Casalzuigno and work in Ticino, the procedure starts with verifying residency. It is necessary to ensure that the purchase or lease deed complies with local regulations and that the civil‑registry residence is up‑to‑date. The next step is the request for Permit G, the document that authorizes cross‑border work. This permit is issued by the competent Swiss authority, often in coordination with the Italian authorities. It is important to submit the application early, as processing times may vary. The required documentation includes the employment contract, proof of residence in Casalzuigno and identity documents.
Once Permit G is obtained, tax management becomes automatic regarding withholding tax, but the filing of the income‑tax return in Italy remains the responsibility. The tax credit must be entered in the CE section of the 730 form. Those living in Casalzuigno must keep all Swiss pay slips to verify that the withholdings correspond to the applicable rates. In case of discrepancies, they can report them to the AFC/ESTV or to the cantonal tax services. It is not advisable to rely on approximate calculations for the return; it is better to use reliable calculation tools to estimate the net amount and the taxes due.
### Tools and resources for the cross‑border worker To evaluate the opportunity of moving, it is useful to compare the cost of living between the two countries. The cost of housing, utilities and services in Casalzuigno can be significantly lower than in Ticino. However, commuting expenses such as fuel or public‑transport tickets must be added to the budget. For those uncertain about the economic convenience, a CHF/EUR exchange‑rate comparator can help estimate real purchasing power. Moreover, for those who wish to simulate their net salary after Swiss withholdings and Italian tax, the tax calculator is the most effective tool. This tool allows entering contract parameters and obtaining a detailed estimate of the monthly net.
Choosing to live in Casalzuigno and work in Ticino is a multi‑year decision that requires analysis. Advantages include the higher salary and the quality of Swiss public services, while disadvantages may involve travel time and bureaucratic complexity. To maintain constant control over one’s fiscal and social‑security situation, it is essential to regularly update personal information. Simulate your net salary with the tax calculator (nav:calculator) to see how much will remain in your account after all withholdings and taxes foreseen by the New Cross‑Border Agreement and the 1976 Convention.

item.title: Stadler Rail focuses on Kazakhstan: 53 million investments
item.description: The Turgovian manufacturer Stadler Rail invests 25 million francs in the Astana plant to start the production of aluminium crates.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Stadler Rail invests 25 million francs in the Astana plant - Another 100 jobs created and new production in Astana - Total investment of at least 53 million francs between 2023 and 2031
## Key facts - **What**: Investment for railway plant and aluminum carbody production - When: Period from 2023 to 2031 - Where: Astana, Kazakhstan - Who: Stadler Rail, Thurgau-based railway manufacturer - Amount: 25 million francs in immediate investment, 53 million total
The Thurgau-based railway manufacturer Stadler Rail has announced an investment of 25 million francs directly allocated to its plant located in Astana. This large-scale industrial operation allows for the creation of another 100 local jobs and gives rise to the first highly automated production of aluminum carbodies for railway vehicles in the entire Central Asia region. The official announcement was issued through a press release released today by the company itself, highlighting the strategic scope of the overseas production expansion project. Inside the Kazakh production site, new workshops are planned specifically dedicated to the welding and painting of various structural elements of the trains. Currently, the industrial structure employs about 650 people in the territory of Kazakhstan. Local specialists are trained directly for the new complex tasks at Stadler Rail's operational headquarters located in Europe, thus guaranteeing a high quality and technological standard.
### Operations and production lines in Astana The Astana plant already plays a central role today, handling numerous phases of train production. Among other things, railway carbodies, dedicated electrical equipment, undercarriage components and bogies are manufactured at this site, alongside the assembly and commissioning activities of the railway vehicles. With this new expansion phase, Stadler Rail's stated objective is to significantly increase local added value. Overall, the industrial group aims to invest at least 53 million francs in Kazakhstan in the period between 2023 and 2031, further consolidating its international production presence in a key market for the supply of advanced rolling stock meeting the needs of local and foreign customers. The announcement of the new investments made by the Thurgau-based group found an immediate response also on international financial markets and stock exchanges. On the stock market, the Stadler Rail share recorded a gain of almost 3%, settling at around 29 francs per single share. Analyzing the financial trend of the stock on the stock market, it is observed that since the beginning of January the price has risen by 35%, while over the previous twelve months the overall calculated increase stands at 41%. However, it should be remembered that at the time of its initial stock market landing in April 2019, the stock was traded at a value of 43 francs, highlighting the historical fluctuations that have characterized the stock market journey of the Thurgau company over the years.
### Historical origins and industrial profile of the group To fully understand the current structure of the company, it is useful to retrace its industrial roots. Stadler Rail traces its historical origins back to the engineering firm founded by Ernst Stadler in 1942 in Zurich. Today the company has its main headquarters located in Bussnang, in the canton of Thurgau (TG). The enterprise is engaged in the manufacture of a wide range of rolling stock ranging from high-speed trains to regional convoys, including trams and vehicles destined for underground systems. These are modern vehicles that also circulate regularly on Swiss and Ticino railway lines. The industrial group has a total of 18'000 employees distributed globally, of which about 6'000 units work directly in Switzerland. Regarding financial data relating to business volume, in 2025 the company achieved a total turnover of 3.7 billion francs, confirming its economic solidity and strategic relevance within the Swiss manufacturing and metalworking sector.

The group's financial planning, which foresees total resources of at least CHF 53 million between 2023 and 2031, testifies to a strategic vision aimed at increasing local added value and optimising construction processes for rolling stock destined for international rail networks.

## In a nutshell - Nomination of Sergio Savoia for Forward with Ticino&Lavoro - Reactions on social media and controversy with haters - Clarification on the definition of pensioner
## Key facts - **What**: Political candidacy and responses to criticism - When: September 2026 - Where: Lugano and Canton Ticino - Who: Sergio Savoia

## In brief - Open day at the plant on September 19 - Mandatory reservations via the Eventbrite platform - District heating plant active in Varese since 1992
## Key facts - **What**: Extraordinary opening of the district heating plant - When: Saturday, September 19 from 9 am all day long - Where: Plant at via Ottorino Rossi 19 in Varese - Who: Gruppo Acinque and Acinque Tecnologie - Amount: 63 GWh of thermal energy delivered in 2025 - Capacity: Network of 16 kilometers serving about 12,000 equivalent apartments
The appointment with Impianti Aperti returns to the province of Varese, the series of free guided tours to the facilities of the Acinque Group which takes place throughout the year across all territories served by the multi-utility and which in the last edition involved about 700 citizens. On Saturday, September 19, starting from 9 am all day long, the doors of the Varese district heating plant, located at via Ottorino Rossi 19, will open. This is the beating heart of the network that runs through the capital city, an energy system active in the city since 1992. To participate in the tour, reservations are required via the Eventbrite.it platform. The initiative allows citizens to get a close-up look at the technological and professional heritage of the group.
### Objectives of the Open Plants initiative Acinque's choice to annually open a selection of its plants has a dual purpose. On the one hand, it aims to raise citizens' awareness on energy issues and the value of natural resources to promote their conscious use. On the other hand, it aims to showcase the technological and professional heritage of the group that daily creates economic spillover effects for the local territories. The Varese event represents the first stop of this visiting program which continues in other locations in Lombardy in the following weeks, offering all interested parties the opportunity to discover the inner workings of large local energy infrastructures and to understand the industrial production processes managed by the multi-utility in the provincial and regional territory. The Varese district heating system boasts a history of over thirty years, having been operational in the city for more than three decades. The plant supplies heat to over 150 users, which include not only residential condominiums but also commercial businesses, industrial activities, and public buildings located in the south-east area of Varese. Among the main beneficiaries of this energy service are the University of Insubria campus, the Fondazione Molina, the Municipality, and the Varese hospital. The distribution network, entirely managed by Acinque Tecnologie, branches out into the urban fabric for a total length of 16 kilometers, guaranteeing thermal coverage for approximately 12,000 equivalent apartments distributed throughout the city area.
### Integration with renewable sources and cogeneration The Varese system is powered by heat produced by the cogeneration plant in Via Ottorino Rossi 19. Through cogeneration engines, the plant is able to produce electricity and simultaneously recover the thermal energy released during the thermodynamic process. This combined production allows for a significant reduction in fuel for power supply, achieved by recovering energy that would otherwise be dispersed into the atmosphere as waste. Thanks to this cogeneration process, during 2025 the plant supplied 63 GWh of thermal energy.
A distinctive peculiarity of the Varese system lies in the presence of a solar thermal plant that integrates the heat production of the plant by exploiting a renewable source such as the sun. Solar thermal panels can produce 450 MWh of thermal energy in a year, exactly equal to the domestic hot water requirement of 150 apartments. This contribution makes it possible to avoid the use of fossil fuels for 43 toe and prevents the emission of 108 tons of CO2 into the atmosphere every year.

item.title: Speedaf in Switzerland: 50,000 packages per day
item.description: Speedaf, a Swiss subsidiary founded in April, aims to handle up to 50,000 shipments per day with centres in Zurich, Bern and Lausanne and headquarters in Freiburg.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Speedaf lands in Switzerland to compete with Posta, Planzer, DPD and DHL. - The Chinese group aims to handle up to 50,000 shipments per day. - Swiss subsidiary founded in April and already operational, headquartered in Fribourg. - 60% is Posta's market share in the parcel sector in 2025.
## Key facts - **What**: Entry of Chinese logistics giant Speedaf into the Swiss parcel market. - When: Subsidiary founded last April, operational within one or two years. - Where: Legal headquarters in Fribourg, distribution centres planned in Zurich, Bern and Lausanne. - Who: Speedaf, with the support of founding shareholders including ZTO Express. - Amount: Internal model estimated at 1.80 francs per parcel, with a profit threshold of 1.20 francs.
Competition looming in Switzerland for Posta and other established carriers such as Planzer, DPD and DHL: Chinese logistics giant Speedaf is building a network across the country. It could capture a market share quickly, within one or two years. The group, already active in over thirty countries across Asia, the Middle East and Africa, wants to open a sorting centre to manage a volume of up to 50,000 shipments per day and regional distribution centres in Zurich, Bern and Lausanne. Speedaf's Swiss subsidiary was founded only in April and is already operational, having indicated a staff representative to the Awp agency. Parcels with the conspicuous orange brand are already visible in front of house doors. Considerable quantities are already being moved, the source says, without providing concrete figures. The company has its legal headquarters in Fribourg and is recruiting staff. The central sorting centre should cover about 4,000 square metres, while the regional distribution centres should each measure about 500 square metres. For the larger structure, according to rumours Speedaf has set its sights on the Härkingen region (SO), where Posta already operates. In the delivery area the group wants to build a network that also relies on fleet operators and independent partners. The goal is a capillary last‑mile delivery. The company apparently aims to win over Swiss online retailers, brick‑and‑mortar traders, as well as small and medium‑sized enterprises, thereby directly impacting the business of established operators. Speedaf arrives in the Confederation with an important advantage: access to large volumes of parcels from Chinese e‑commerce. The group, founded in 2019, also has ties to a heavyweight of the Chinese sector: among its founding shareholders is ZTO Express, one of China’s largest parcel services. ZTO is likewise pushing its international activities: last April its air‑cargo division inaugurated the first freight link directly to Europe, linking Hong Kong to Budapest.
### Organisational and logistics structure
The expansion details outline a capillary strategy across Swiss territory. The creation of regional distribution centres in strategic hubs such as Zurich, Bern and Lausanne shows the intention to quickly cover the country’s main urban agglomerations. The recruitment drive is already underway and the choice of the Härkingen region in the canton of Solothurn for the central sorting hub of four thousand square metres mirrors the logistics map already exploited by historic competitors. The use of third‑party fleets and independent partners allows Speedaf to lighten initial fixed costs, aiming for a flexible network focused on final‑door delivery. Direct involvement of ZTO Express provides a significant financial and operational backbone internationally, capable of sustaining the initial market‑penetration phase in Switzerland. How much Speedaf is aggressively calculating for entry into the Swiss market is shown by an internal planning template posted on LinkedIn by a company manager. For a selected delivery area Speedaf is assumed to receive CHF 1.80 per parcel. The profit threshold is just under 1.20 francs. There would therefore be just over 60 cents of profit left per submission. These are numbers that raise the ears of the sector: the calculated profit threshold would be very low and rather unrealistic, says a representative of the branch in statements made to AWP. In his opinion, however, the new competitor should not be underestimated. Chinese competition needs to be taken seriously, especially if you look at what is currently happening in the European automotive industry. It is also remarkable that a foreign supplier with direct access to large quantities of shipments from China builds its own Swiss network. In this way, it is not excluded that Speedaf will grow rapidly: within one or two years the company could rise among the large suppliers of the Swiss parcel market. Decisive will be to see how much financial wind the company has. Success will also depend on the quality of delivery. The Post Office, as the dominant operator, carefully observes the new competitor, but is sure of itself. The company has successfully faced intense competition in the parcel market for many years, a spokesperson said.

Attention remains high also on the union and regulatory front, where the request for a sector-wide collective contract is invoked by historic market leaders to avoid competitive distortions based solely on lowering management and labor costs. ## In brief - Pognana Lario is located on the eastern shore of the Como branch of Lake Como. - The journey to the Brogeda customs requires passing through Como. - New Agreement in force since January 1, 2024, with a €10,000 tax-free allowance.
## Key facts - **What**: Living on the lake and working as a cross-border worker in Canton Ticino - When: New Agreement valid from January 1, 2024 (Law 83 of 13/6/2023) - Where: Pognana Lario, Province of Como and border crossings towards Chiasso - Who: Cross-border workers with a G permit residing in the border zone - Amount: Tax-free allowance for new cross-border workers at €10,000; exemption for old ones at €7,500
Pognana Lario is situated along the Larian provincial road between Como and Bellagio, offering an open view of the lake and a quiet residential context. Those who choose to settle in this village to travel every working day to Canton Ticino must set their road itinerary by descending towards Como and then heading for the customs of Ponte Chiasso or the motorway at Brogeda. Travel times depend heavily on morning traffic conditions along the coastal road and in crossing the provincial capital before reaching Switzerland.
### Road system and connections to the border To reach the main work destinations in Mendrisiotto or Lugano, the classic itinerary involves leaving Pognana Lario on the SP 583 towards Como. Once past the city, the route continues towards the Brogeda crossing for the A2 motorway junction or through the city customs. During peak hours, the main bottleneck is represented by the access points to Como, where the vehicle flow from the lakeshore converges. Monitoring customs crossing times via updates on [border waiting times](nav:border) is useful for planning early morning departures and avoiding significant delays at the border. Choosing Pognana Lario offers advantages in terms of tranquility and panoramic views, but requires careful evaluation of the daily commute. Compared to other municipalities in the Como belt, real estate costs for purchasing or renting can be more affordable for an equivalent surface area and panoramic view, partly offsetting road transport expenses.
### Fiscal framework between Switzerland and Italy On the tax and social security front, G-permit workers must distinguish their status based on their date of hire. The New Cross-Border Agreement, signed on 23 December 2020 and entered into force on 1 January 2024 following its ratification with Law 83 of 13 June 2023, governs the treatment between the two States, integrating the historic Double Taxation Agreement of 9 December 1976. Withholding tax on employment income is levied only in Switzerland by the cantonal administration and the FTA/ESTV. In Italy, no double taxation occurs because the foreign tax credit is applied in section CE of the tax return. For those who entered the Swiss market before 17 July 2023, the transitional regime applies until 2033 with an exemption of €7,500, in addition to the tax refunds distributed to border municipalities. For new cross-border commuters hired after that date, an allowance of €10,000 applies to total income, followed by progressive taxation under IRPEF brackets (23% up to €28,000, 35% between €28,001 and €50,000, 43% above €50,000). The first step is to change residence at the municipal registry, promptly communicating the new territorial location to the Swiss employer for the updating of the G permit. From the point of view of Swiss social security, the paycheck includes the mandatory deductions: AVS/AI/IPG equal to 5.3% borne by the worker, AD/AC unemployment insurance at 1.1% up to the maximum of CHF 148'200, LAINF accident coverage between 0.7% and 1.5% and the second LPP pillar with scalar rates from 7% to 18% based on the age group from 25 years.
